simple.meaning: קְלֹקֵל (qᵉlôqêl) is a Hebrew object word meaning “insubstantial.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Numbers 21:5. The surrounding context includes wilderness, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קְלֹקֵל (H7052) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H7052. qeloqel קְלֹקֵל adjective contemptible, worthless (compare Ol § 189 f Ba NB 160 ); — הַקּ ׳בַּלֶּחֶם Num 21:5 (JE).

occurrences.englishText: The people spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread, there is no water, and our soul loathes this disgusting food!”
